paragraphs: Yosef Katnuta: when he died, the pious ceased. Eglah Arufah, mishnah 15, page 49: why? Because he was the essence and root of the pious, since a thing’s root and beginning are small. Accordingly, he would be after Rabbi Yose HaKohen, Rabbi Yehudah ben Bava, and Rabbi Yehudah bar Ilai, who were pious; see Isi ben Akiva above. Zohar, Bereshit, at the locator על״ד: a philosopher from the nations asked Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai: ‘You say that your God rules all the heights of heaven,’ and so forth. ‘It is written, “Among all the nations’ sages there is none like You,”’ and so forth, ‘but among Israel’s sages there is,’ and so forth. He replied: ‘Who revives the dead and brings rain, except the Holy One, blessed be He? Yet we find Elijah and Elisha revived the dead and brought rain,’ and so forth. He went and converted at Kefar Shachalaya, and they called him Yosef Katina. He learned much Torah and was among that place’s wise and righteous. End quotation. At the printed reference ובספ״ק דל״ב א׳ it says: ‘The introduction to Zohar, Bereshit, appears to show that he converted in Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai’s days,’ and so forth. It is not in the introduction, but in the Zohar passage above.
